name: Stop by text: 'Happy, stop everything', and lock one person out
description: Either parent can text one exact phrase and Happy stops: no agent runs and no tool calls until Tony switches it back on at the Mac. Texts from scheduled jobs that use no model (the weather and page watchers) are cancelled only on a best-effort basis until Tony also switches the scheduler off. A second phrase stops Happy answering one person's handle, for a lost or stolen phone.
example: Jordan texts 'Happy, stop everything' when briefs start arriving twice. Tony texts 'Happy, lock out Jordan' after her phone is left in a taxi.
how: In-house plugin. before_dispatch claims the exact phrase from an adult's handle and writes a kill file (everything) or a suspended file (one person's handles). The stop is enforced where hooks fail closed: before_agent_run blocks agent runs before the model reads the prompt, and before_tool_call blocks tools; message_sending cancels scheduled announce texts as a best-effort extra. Levels that need no plugin code, done by Tony: `cron.enabled: false`, then `openclaw gateway stop`. Lifting a stop or a lock-out is CLI-only. For a stolen phone the operator step still has to follow: remove the handle from family.json5 and redeploy, which is the only thing that ends that handle's approver rights; `openclaw devices revoke` if the phone ran the OpenClaw app; Find My Lost Mode on the phone side.
caveats: The phrase matcher is a claim hook and message_sending is a delivery hook: both log and continue when their handler throws or times out, so the stop must not live only there.
Command jobs make no agent run, so their announce texts can only be caught by message_sending (as read from the bundled code, not yet tested); the dependable stop for those is the scheduler switch.
/stop (OCL-06) ends one answer in one chat; this stops everything.
For a stolen phone, 'stop everything' already works as the blunt version; the lock-out phrase only keeps Happy answering the other parent in the meantime.
A locked phone already stops most misuse. The lock-out covers a phone taken while unlocked or a passcode seen over a shoulder.
Either adult can lock the other out, and Tony undoes it at the Mac. If whoever holds the phone sends the phrase first, the real owner needs the CLI.
A lock-out stops replies and texts to that person, not their scheduled jobs; pause those too with the mute and vacation controls in G001.
Keep both phrases out of Happy's own help text and replies.
corrections: 'Freeze every outbound write' is fail-closed only for tool calls. The phrase matcher and the message_sending check both log and continue when their handler throws or times out, so a broken plugin lets the phrase reach the model and lets scheduled announce texts out. The levels that do not depend on plugin code are the scheduler switch and stopping the Gateway.
unverified: That before_agent_run fires for scheduled agent-turn jobs on this build; test with a throwaway job.
Whether switching the scheduler off stops a job already running, and whether switching it back needs a restart (the hot-reload table says no; the automation troubleshooting page says restart).
How plugin code running as the happy user would change the scheduler setting, given the config repo is read-only to it; the kill file may be the only chat-triggered level.
What the sender sees when before_agent_run blocks a run and no replacement message is set.
Whether a tapback from a suspended handle can still resolve a pending approval, and whether owner-only slash commands from that handle are parsed before the plugin's hooks run.

The Shortcut and ntfy-button triggers from the 9 Oct entry: where an ntfy action request originates, and whether it can reach the Gateway over Tailscale, was not confirmed, so the text phrase is the only confirmed trigger.
safety: Both phrases can only narrow what Happy does; nothing in the chat path can add a sender or switch anything back on. A chat lock-out leaves the handle on channels.imessage.allowFrom, which is also the approver list, so that person's agent runs and tool calls must be blocked by the fail-closed hooks until Tony removes the handle and redeploys.

name: When the model is down: an honest notice, jobs that need no model, and an optional same-vendor fallback
description: When the cloud model has an incident, Happy today answers with a raw error or not at all. With this, when errors go on, each parent gets one plain 'the model is down' line and later a 'back' line, and the alerts that need no model keep working: the weather watch, the stop phrase, and any fixed reminder Tony has set up as a no-model job (bin day). As an option Tony has to decide on, the vendor's lower-cost model answers that turn and the chat shows a one-line notice saying so; OpenClaw's security guidance warns against running an agent that has tools on a smaller model, so this part stays off unless he accepts that.
example: Trigger: gpt-6-sol returns server errors for ten minutes at 07:00 while the morning brief is due.
how:
Today each person agent is generated with `model.fallbacks: []`, and the docs say an agent's primary is strict unless its model object lists fallbacks, so after the built-in retries a failure surfaces as a terminal error that keeps the provider's HTTP status. Three steps. (1) Fallback (optional; it needs Tony's decision, because OpenClaw's prompt-injection guidance says not to run tool-enabled agents on smaller model tiers): add gpt-6-luna on the same per-person provider id as the single fallback for

-main, one line in gen-family, since both models are already in that agent's modelPolicy.allow under the same key and store setting. The docs say a fallback is used for that turn only and a one-line notice is shown in direct chats. Mail and kid agents keep `fallbacks: []` as the roadmap requires. This covers model-scoped incidents and rate limits, not a vendor-wide outage. (2) Model-free jobs: the weather watch (F018) is specified as a `--command-argv` job and the stop phrase (G005) is a `before_dispatch` claim, so both work through an outage. Timed reminders (F007) and the briefs are `--message` jobs, which the docs define as model-backed agent turns, so they fail with the model; a fixed-text reminder that must not be missed, such as bin day, has to be created as a command job that prints its line. A scheduled agent turn can also carry its own `--fallbacks` list. (3) Outage notice: extend the health watch (G008) so that when the existing error-ratio alert has fired for N minutes, a host script sends each parent one fixed line and later one 'back' line by a model-free send: `openclaw message send` to the pinned family handles, or a command job with announce delivery. The catalog's usual host path, `openclaw agent --deliver`, runs an agent turn and so cannot announce a model outage. `openclaw models status --check` is not the detector: its own docs say a clean exit does not prove a request will succeed.
depends_on: decision: whether the vendor's lower-cost model may answer for a parent's main agent when the usual one fails, against OpenClaw's guidance not to run tool-enabled agents on smaller models (the notice and the no-model jobs do not wait on this)
G008 health watch and the O1 error-ratio alert
G009 family delivery (for the notice)
caveats: OpenClaw's prompt-injection guidance says not to use smaller or cheaper model tiers for agents that have tools or read outside content, and each parent's main agent does both (reminders, lists, family delivery, photos and PDFs). The fallback here is the vendor's lower-cost model, so allowing it is a decision and not a default; without it an outage means the plain notice and no answers until the usual model is back.

OpenAI's status history listed 39 incidents in September 2026 and 23 in the first ten days of October across all its products. Most do not touch the API models Happy uses, but some did, for example 'elevated error rates across API models' on 17 Sep.
An answer from the smaller model can be worse than the usual one; the fallback notice tells the parent which model answered.
No fallback to a second vendor: it would need another vendor's key and a new privacy decision, and the local route is the skipped M2, so a vendor-wide outage still means no answers until it ends.
An API key that hits its monthly cap looks like an outage until the month ends; the fixed line should say 'limit reached' when that is the cause.
If the Mac, the home internet or iMessage is what failed, nothing here helps. The dead-man alert is then the only signal and it goes to Tony.
A scheduled brief that fails is simply missed unless the job's retry settings say otherwise.
safety: No new data path. The fallback uses the same provider id, key and store:false setting, and the notice is a fixed string to pinned family recipients. Mail and kid agents stay strict, so their content can never move to another model by accident.
unverified: The exact text a parent sees on iMessage when every candidate fails; the docs describe it, it was not triggered in this run.
Whether gpt-6-luna stays healthy during typical gpt-6-sol incidents.
Whether command jobs deliver normally while model calls are failing; nothing suggests otherwise but it was not tested.
Whether 'openclaw message send' passes through the same recipient-pinning hook as the agent's message tool; if it does not, the host script must hard-code the family handles from the registry.

name: Notification policy: daily cap, quiet hours, priority classes and job tags, plus snooze, mute and vacation mode by chat
description: Caps how many unprompted texts each parent gets in a day, stops non-urgent ones outside allowed hours and labels each one so you know which job sent it. A text stopped by the cap or the hours is dropped, not sent later, so scheduled jobs are timed inside the allowed hours in the first place. Either parent can text 'mute until 3' or 'we are away next week', and briefs, bin reminders and routines pause for that window while urgent alerts still arrive. The pause is dependable for the briefs and other jobs that check it themselves, and best effort for timed reminders, which can only be stopped at delivery.
example: Jordan texts: 'We are away next week.' Briefs and bin reminders stop for the week; an urgent alert still arrives.
how: Policy (G001): an in-house plugin with `before_tool_call` on `message` (fails closed) and a `message_sending` cancel for `--announce` deliveries (fails open on error); counters live in the household store, and schedules are generated inside the allowed windows in the first place. Pause (G002): a paused-until row in the same store. A job that holds the store tool reads the row first and answers `NO_REPLY`. A job that cannot read it, such as a timed reminder, which runs with an empty tool list (F007), is paused by the plugin's delivery hook instead: the hook reads the same row and cancels the text. For a long absence a host helper can also run `openclaw automations disable|enable <job-id>`, and `cron.enabled: false` pauses everything. The policy's priority classes decide which alerts still pass during a mute. OpenClaw also lets a command owner (a sender listed in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`) ask the agent to change an existing automation by chat; that is not the route used here (see caveats).
caveats: Each iPhone can already silence the night on a schedule, so what Happy adds is the daily cap, the urgent or not-urgent split, the label and the pause by chat.

The delivery hook can only rewrite or cancel a text, so one stopped by the daily cap or by quiet hours is dropped, not delivered later; holding texts and releasing them in a batch would need a queue of the plugin's own, which is not designed. Scheduled jobs are therefore timed inside the allowed hours, and the hook is the backstop.

It is not a hard gate for scheduled texts: the message_sending hook that sees `--announce` deliveries lets the message through if the plugin throws or times out, and only the agent's own message tool is gated fail-closed.
The reading of the announce path comes from bundled JavaScript and not a doc page, so confirm it with a throwaway hook before relying on either hook.
No doc lists a job id on message_sending, so each job may have to write its own tag into the text.
No built-in quiet hours or priority classes were found in OpenClaw, so keeping urgent alerts on during a mute depends on this plugin.
The household store does not exist yet, so the counters and the paused-until row are a design and not an installed feature.
The fixed emergency reply (CRT-13) answers an inbound text and must never be held back by quiet hours, caps or a mute.

Timed reminders run with an empty tool list (F007), so a reminder job cannot check the pause itself; its text is stopped only by the delivery hook, which is the best-effort side. A mute is therefore dependable for the briefs and other jobs that read the row themselves and best effort for reminders. Because a stopped text is dropped and not sent late, a one-off reminder that falls inside a mute would be lost, so one-off reminders a parent set belong in a class that passes; a recurring one such as the bins reminder can pause, because the next one comes round anyway.

Switching a job off by chat is open only to a command owner, which is Tony's handle alone today (adding Jordan is the open decision recorded on F007). OpenClaw's page gives that sender's agent the power to update, run or remove any job on the Gateway, not only to pause one, and a job changed that way no longer matches the registry (G003). The paused-until row is the route both parents use, and it changes no job.
corrections: reply_payload_sending does not cover --announce on the installed build: the scheduler's announce path sends without a reply-payload hook descriptor and the outbound stage skips that hook when none is supplied. message_sending is the hook that sees those deliveries (the G005 wording already uses it), and it fails open on handler error, so it is a best-effort gate.

The 9 Oct note said switching jobs off needs operator.admin and so cannot be done from

-main; the installed docs also let a sender listed in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` ask the agent to disable an existing automation by chat.
unverified: The announce-path reading comes from bundled JavaScript, not a doc page; confirm with a throwaway hook before relying on either hook.
How the hook learns which job produced a text; no doc lists a job id on message_sending, so the job may have to write its own tag into the text.
Whether a scheduled iPhone Do Not Disturb can silence only Happy's thread; Apple's page confirmed scheduling and allowed people, not per-contact silencing.
The home-store plugin does not exist yet; the paused-until row is a design, not an installed feature.
safety: Both halves only hold back or pause Happy's own unprompted texts; neither adds a recipient, a tool or a data source. Urgent classes keep passing during a mute, and switching everything off stays an operator action.

name: Local classifier calls (decision_evaluate with an on-device ONNX model)
description: A way to ask a small on-device model a yes/no, pick-one or score question (does this text look like a bank statement, is this school email a closure or delay, is this reply fine for an eight-year-old) and get a typed answer with a probability, with no cloud call. It is a building block, not something the family sees, and no card needs it yet: it could later replace the pattern match in the document privacy gate (part of F002), sort closure mail in the school digest (F051) and, much later, sit in front of the kids filters (F072), which still need their own child-safety model. It does not depend on the skipped local-LLM milestone.
example: Trigger: the school-mail reader's hook asks one Boolean question about a new email's subject and first lines (is this a closure, delay or early dismissal?); only a probability above the threshold is passed on at the next sweep instead of waiting for the 16:00 digest (F051).
how:
Release 2026.9.7 adds the decisionModel role and the core decision_evaluate tool, and plugins can call the same runtime from a hook through api.runtime.decisions.evaluate. The local provider is the @openclaw/onnx plugin, installed pinned to the Gateway version (npm:@openclaw/onnx@2026.9.7): zero-shot classifier presets on CPU in a separate worker process, with models fetched only by an explicit download command and checked against fixed hashes. Config is agents.defaults.decisionModel (or per agent) plus plugins.entries.onnx. Call it from the in-house hooks (the privacy gate in F002, the F051 school-mail reader, later the F072 kids filters) rather than granting the tool to

-main.
depends_on: The co-versioned plugin release pinned at install (npm:@openclaw/onnx@2026.9.7), proven to load and pass its probe command on a test profile before any gate relies on it
A small labelled test set per question, so false positives and misses are measured before a gate relies on it
caveats: The installed 2026.9.7 docs still call the ONNX and TypeSafe plugins unpublished candidates, but the npm registry lists an @openclaw/onnx 2026.9.7 build whose requirement is openclaw 2026.9.7 or later. The latest tag (2026.10.1) needs a newer Gateway, so the version must be pinned at install. The plugin is weeks old; treat it as experimental.
These are generic zero-shot classifiers, not child-safety models; they can score and shortlist, but a kids deployment still needs its own evaluation and a second gate.
There is no fallback to the chat model when the decision provider is unavailable, and an unavailable result is not a 'no', so every gate has to fail closed.
The other provider, TypeSafe's hosted model, is a cloud service and out of scope.

Apple's on-device model (the bundled apple-fm plugin) is not a substitute today: it is documented only as a setup and utility model for short internal tasks such as session titles, and none of the installed pages that mention it describe a classification use.
Each encoded input, rubric included, must fit 512 tokens and longer input is rejected rather than truncated, so a gate has to send a subject and first lines, or chunk a document itself.
Returned probabilities are model estimates, not calibrated; thresholds have to come from the labelled test set.
safety: This strengthens the architecture: the decision runs locally and returns a typed value rather than prose, and the hook, not the model, applies the threshold; the docs say results do not grant permission to act. Hostile text can still shift a score, so a classifier is a filter in front of a hard rule, never the rule itself. No data leaves the Mac.
unverified: Whether @openclaw/onnx 2026.9.7 installs and loads cleanly on this 2026.9.7 host; the installed docs predate its publication and describe only a source-checkout route
Classifier accuracy on this family's school mail and on kids' questions
Memory and CPU use of the worker process
Which host the model download command fetches weights from and which egress rule it needs

example: Jordan texts: 'Will it rain during Saturday's 10 o'clock game?' Happy answers with the hourly chance of rain from 9 to noon and any active alert for home.
how: Extend the in-house home_weather plugin: follow forecastHourly from /points, add alert id, read snowfallAmount from the raw gridpoint endpoint; keep the api.weather.gov host pin.
caveats: Apple's Weather app can already send a notification when rain or snow is about to start or stop, and for government-issued severe-weather alerts at a saved location; Apple notes this is not offered in every country or region. This tool earns its place as the weather feed for the briefs (F014) and the trip planner (F028), which need an hourly rain window, and for questions asked inside a Happy conversation. The weather watch (F018) polls the alerts feed with its own script and does not depend on this tool.
The National Weather Service hourly forecast reaches seven days ahead, so a question about a game further out gets no hour-by-hour answer until the date comes into range.
unverified: The snowfall field name and units were seen only in the OpenAPI description of the raw gridpoint endpoint, not in a live response.
NWS publishes no numeric rate limit, so the 10-minute cache is a design choice rather than an NWS rule.
Whether those Weather notifications are offered and switched on for the home location on each parent's iPhone: the Apple page read was the Mac Weather guide, and the iPhone guide did not render.

name: School mailbox with an isolated reader and a weekday 16:00 digest
description: A separate mailbox registered with school, PTA, coaches and the lunch system is read by an isolated, memory-less reader, so no parent's private inbox is touched. Weekday afternoons both parents get a five-line text of the day's school and activity mail with dates spelled out, a dated to-do list, and one line per child from the school platforms' own summary emails where the school uses them. A parent who wants a day-before reminder for a line asks their own agent for it.
example: Trigger: weekdays at 16:00. Text: 'School mail today: picture day is Thursday 15 October, order form due Wednesday 14 October; PTA meeting moved to Tuesday 20 October at 7 pm; lunch balance is low.' Jordan then texts Happy: 'remind me Tuesday evening about the picture day form.'
how: Mailbox (F051): the bundled `imap` plugin on a new mailbox (iCloud needs `watch.mode: "interval"`), a sender allowlist that includes both parents for forwards, and a tool-less reader. The plugin cannot text a person by itself, so reaching the parents needs a hook-pinned `message` tool or a scheduled sweep. Digest (F056): `automations create '0 16 * * 1-5' --agent school-mail --session isolated --announce --to <chat>` with `--tools school-mail-ro__*`; the read MCP is `gog mcp` (Gmail) or a himalaya wrapper (iCloud). Setup done once by a parent, per platform: ParentSquare posts set to Digest with email on, PowerSchool's scheduled emails and Balance Alert sent to the mailbox, Google Classroom guardian summaries, the lunch service's low-balance alert, library notices; each sender goes on the allowlist.
caveats: Pick the mailbox provider with the password in mind: the plugin signs in with a mailbox password only, which on Gmail means a Google app password that Google does not recommend, while OpenClaw's guide names Fastmail and iCloud.

Each school system has to accept an extra guardian address, a manual chore per system, and auto-forwarding from a parent's Gmail may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
The reader gets body text and attachment file names only, so PDF or image newsletters and flyer attachments are not read.

Urgent alerts are not this digest's job, since the school's own alerts reach the parents' phones first; the reader keeps one backup rule (a closure, delay or early-dismissal message from an allowlisted school sender is passed on at the next sweep, not held until 16:00), and sorting urgent from routine on real district mail is untested.

PowerSchool emails carry grades and attendance and Classroom summaries carry assignment titles: these are a child's education records and they reach the cloud model under store:false, which is why the card is rated medium risk.
Classroom summaries (missing and upcoming work, no grades) arrive only if the school uses Classroom and the teacher switches them on, and the guardian invitation expires after 120 days.
One job appears to take one delivery target, so two parents need two jobs or the parents' group chat, and the iCloud read path likely needs an in-house himalaya wrapper.

For a school or team app that sends no email, try the app's own email notifications into this mailbox first and a parent's screenshot to Happy second; Canvas and ClassDojo have no verified email path.

The reminder step is not wired end to end. The reader that writes the digest holds no reminder or store tool, on purpose, because it reads untrusted mail, and it is untested whether the parent's own agent, which receives any reply, can see the digest text. Until that is tested, a parent names the line when asking their own agent for a reminder. Giving the reader a write to the household store would let text from a school email reach the parents' private agents, so that route needs its own review first.

The sender list lives in family.json5 and changes only with a reviewed deploy, so a parent who needs a new coach or teacher added asks Tony. The mail plugin logs a rejected message without its subject or body, so a mail that did not show up can be traced in the gateway log.
A calendar link that a school platform offers is subscribed in the family calendar (F009), not read by this reader.
corrections: 'IMAP passes body text only' is slightly off: the plugin's prompt also lists attachment file names (dist/extensions/imap/index.js:55735). Contents of attached PDFs or images are still not passed, so flyer attachments remain unread.
'school-mail-ro MCP is gog (Gmail)' needs no wrapper code on the Gmail path: upstream gogcli ships a read-only stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`).
The built-in scheduling tool is listed as `automations`, with `cron` kept as an alias (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:73).
unverified: Whether the district, PTA, coaches and lunch system each accept an extra or shared guardian address; this is a manual chore per system.

Auto-forwarding school mail from a parent's Gmail by filter may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check (Google's forwarding guidance says forwarded mail often fails SPF); DKIM survival was not tested, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
An iCloud+ custom-domain address with this plugin was not tested; Apple documents the IMAP host and app-specific passwords, not this combination.

Whether himalaya has an MCP mode; its README does not mention one, so the iCloud path likely needs an in-house wrapper. The README also says native keyring support was removed in v2, so its password comes from a command.
That one job takes exactly one delivery target (hence two jobs or one group chat for two parents); I saw single-target examples only.
Groups are off today, so a family group chat target needs the iMessage group allowlist switched on first.
Which platforms this family's district uses, and each platform's exact sender address and authentication result.
Whether the school uses Google Classroom at all, and whether a student can have the school mailbox as an extra guardian next to both parents.
ClassDojo's notification behaviour and Canvas's calendar feed for observers; neither page could be opened.
Whether a parent's reply to the digest reaches an agent that can see the digest text: the digest is announced by the school-mail agent from an isolated run, and replies go to the parent's own agent.
safety: All school mail is untrusted and is read only by the memory-less school-mail agent behind a sender allowlist with verified authentication; that agent has no web or file tools and can only announce to the two parents. Links are relayed only when their domain matches the allowlisted sender. No agent logs in to a school portal and no portal credentials are stored.

name: Childcare coverage planner: no-school days and summer weeks
description: A grid of every weekday the kids have no school (teacher days, breaks, early releases, the ten or so summer weeks) against who covers it: camp, grandparents, a trip, a parent off work. Happy keeps the grid, lists the open cells months ahead, reminds the parents of the registration dates they give it (with a page watch for a camp whose site can be read), and at tax time lists what was paid to which day camp from the receipts a parent sent. School and camp form paperwork is a separate entry (CRT-12).
example: Trigger: first Sunday of February. Happy texts both parents: 'Jordan coverage: 4 of 10 weeks open for the 10-year-old, 6 for the 8-year-old. Two camps you saved open registration this week.'
how:
Inputs: the district calendar (a public feed the family Google Calendar is subscribed to, read through F009, or a photo or PDF through the dates-after-a-yes flow, F010) gives the no-school weekdays; parents add coverage by text. Store: household store rows (F031) keyed by date range and child nickname, with a status (open, pencilled, booked, paid) and a provider name. Jobs: a monthly isolated job on

-main from January to May, and weekly in the four weeks before each break ('--cron'), listing open cells; page watchers for 'registration opens' on camps the parents name (the changed-page watch in F018, created by Tony); options research by the stateless research agent given ages, weeks and a distance only (F019). Parents register and pay themselves. After paying, a parent sends the receipt and Happy records amount and provider. In February it lists day-camp totals per provider and which providers still lack a taxpayer number, because IRS Publication 503 treats day camp, and not overnight camp, as a possible work-related care expense for a child under 13, and asks for the provider's name, address and taxpayer number (Form W-10 is the request form).
depends_on: F031 household store
F009 family calendar subscribed to the district feed, or F010 for a district calendar PDF
F018 page watchers and F019 research agent
F007 reminders
F002 photo and PDF reading, for receipts (its privacy gate screens text PDFs only)
caveats: Most states set the school year near 180 days (28 states in the NCES table), which leaves roughly 80 weekdays a year without school, holidays included. The planner earns its keep only if both parents work on those days.
Camp sites are often script-heavy or bot-walled. Expect 'could not verify' and rely on the parent pasting dates.
Registration is a booking and a payment. Happy stops at the reminder and the link.
The tax list is for the preparer, not tax advice. Whether a camp qualifies depends on facts Happy does not have.
A shared spreadsheet does the grid. The gain here is the reminders, the registration watch and the receipts list for tax time.
safety:
The grid lives with

-main, which holds private data and does not browse. The research agent gets ages, date ranges and distance only, never names, school or address. The page watchers are host scripts with no model (F018) and hold no private data. No registration, booking or payment is performed. A receipt sent as a photo is read by the cloud model like any other photo; the privacy gate in F002 screens text PDFs only.
unverified: Whether the family's district publishes a calendar feed or only a PDF.
That the 2025 edition of Publication 503 carries over unchanged to the 2026 tax year.

name: Enrolment, camp and health-form paperwork kit
description: Every August and every camp season the same documents are asked for again: the immunization record, a recent physical, insurance details, emergency contacts, proof of address. Happy keeps a per-child index of where each document is and when it stops being accepted, warns before a form is due, and, when a school, camp or sports form arrives as a photo or PDF, drafts the answers from the stored family facts as one copy-paste block. The parent fills, signs and submits.
example: Jordan texts: 'Camp forms for both kids are due May 1. What do I still need?'
how:
One Markdown page per child in the shared family folder, indexed through memory.search.extraPaths (F043 step 1). For each document it records where the official copy lives (the pediatric office, the state immunization registry, the filing cabinet), the date on it, and the date it stops being accepted. CDC says it holds no vaccination records and points parents to the child's doctor, the state immunization information system and the school, so the page notes which of those worked last time. A dated row per form in the household store (F031) drives the 'forms due in 14 days' reminder. The date a physical or a record stops being accepted is also listed in the renewals look-ahead (F063), so that 'the physical on file is older than this camp accepts, book a visit' comes from the one list of things running out. The copy-paste block (formerly the health-form helper, F067) is drafted on

-main from a per-child 'form facts' section of the same page when the form arrives as a photo or PDF (F002), under a drafts-only rule in AGENTS.md; the agent has no exec, so it cannot alter or fill in the original form, and ID and policy numbers are left blank for the parent. Scans stay in Files or the paper folder; only the index and the form facts go to Happy.
depends_on: F043 family folder
F031 household store
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments on, for a form sent as a photo or PDF
F007 reminders
caveats: Requirements differ by state, district and camp. Happy tracks what each form asked for last time; it does not know the rules.
The official immunization record has to come from the doctor or the state registry. Happy cannot fetch it, because portal logins are out of scope.
Signing is done by the parent, with the phone's markup tools or on paper. Happy never signs, fills a web form or submits.
An index of where documents are is itself sensitive. Keep ID numbers, policy numbers and certificate numbers out of it.
The form-facts section holds the children's health facts (allergies, medicines, conditions), and they reach the cloud model whenever an answer block is drafted.
The drafts-only rule is a prompt instruction; it holds only because the agent has no tool that could fill in or send a form.

Expiry dates overlap the renewals look-ahead (F063), which already carries a yearly well-visit nudge per child. Keep one list of what is running out there, and keep only the document index, form due dates and the paste-ready answers here.
safety: Index pages hold locations and dates, not the documents or identifiers. The form-facts section does hold the children's health facts, and drafting an answer block sends them to the cloud model under store:false. Both sit in the parents' private agents' search path, nothing is browsed in the same turn, and nothing is sent outside the family. Children's health details stay out of research handoffs.
unverified: Whether this state's immunization registry gives parents direct online access.
Typical validity windows for school and camp physicals; twelve months is often quoted but was not sourced here.

name: Family logistics briefs: evening (19:30), Sunday week-ahead (18:00), weekday morning (07:00)
description: Each parent gets short scheduled texts built from the family calendar and the weather. Sunday to Thursday at 19:30: tomorrow's events, who drives, what to pack and the weather, and nothing when the day is unremarkable. Sunday at 18:00: the week ahead, with early releases, activities, drivers, packing, the weather outlook and open school deadlines. Optionally, weekdays at 07:00: weather and alerts, today's calendar, items due and trash day. Mail stays in its own digests (F051, F016).
example: Sunday to Thursday at 19:30 each parent gets one text: tomorrow's two events and who drives each, 'pack shin guards', and rain after 3.
how:
One isolated job per parent per brief on

-main, all from one template: tools `home_weather` plus the read-only calendar MCP (`

-calendar__*`), no web tools, no `--light-context`, `--tz` set, `--announce --to imessage:`. Schedules: evening `--cron "30 19 * * 0-4"`, week-ahead `--cron "0 18 * * 0"`, morning `--cron "0 7 * * 1-5"`. The routines and gear table lives in AGENTS.md; a run replies `NO_REPLY` to stay silent. The week-ahead and morning legs also read the household store (F031) for items due, trash day and open school deadlines. Email-derived dates for the week-ahead come from a separate

-mail job using `llm-task`, never the same run. Build the evening brief first; the morning brief is the optional one.
caveats: On Sundays the 18:00 week-ahead and the 19:30 evening brief would both arrive within ninety minutes. Either let the Sunday week-ahead carry Monday's detail and run the evening brief Monday to Thursday only (`1-4`), or accept two texts.

The morning leg is the optional one: it needs the household store (F031) for items due and trash day, and the weather plugin returns no sunset, so a sunset line, if wanted, needs a small local calculation.

If the optional 07:00 morning brief and the morning mail digest (F016) are both switched on, a parent gets two texts at 07:00. They cannot be one job, because the mail agent and the parent's main agent are kept apart; move one of them by a quarter of an hour, or leave the morning brief off for a parent who has the mail digest.

Dates taken from mail are not part of the first build: they would come from a separate job on the mail agent (G015, wave C), and how that job hands dates to the brief without passing email text into the parent's main agent still has to be designed. Until then the school deadlines in the week-ahead are rows a parent typed or confirmed (F010).
The National Weather Service forecast reaches seven days ahead, so the Sunday 18:00 weather outlook covers the coming week and no further.

Google's Gemini app can already send a scheduled daily digest of a person's own Google calendar and to-do list (being rolled out gradually to personal accounts, up to ten active actions). What Happy's brief adds is the family's own layer: who drives, what to pack from the routines table, the forecast for home, silence on an unremarkable day, and arrival in the iMessage thread.
unverified: The [T]/[S] driver tag is a family habit the brief depends on, not a product feature; no source can vouch that both adults will keep it up.
gog is not installed, so its flags were checked only against its website, not a binary.
The deadlines input (home-store rows or a sheet) does not exist yet; its shape is a design choice, not a sourced fact.

The catalog passes `home-store__*` in `--tools`; the installed docs document the `<server>__<tool>` prefix only for MCP servers, and home-store is planned as a native plugin, so that glob is untested.
That the NWS forecast endpoints carry no sunrise or sunset field: the opened documentation page does not list one, absence was not proven.
The weather plugin's current fields (12-hour periods, alerts without id, no sunset) were read in ~/src/happy-config/plugins/home-weather/nws.js, which is not one of the two citable source kinds.
safety: Each brief job holds only the weather tool and the read-only calendar tool (plus the household store on the week-ahead and morning legs), has no web tool, and sends its one text only to its own parent. Calendar text can be written by people outside the family (an invitation, a subscribed feed), so it is outside content (see F009); the job's only way out is that one text to its own parent.
